prompts.prompt: Use-case: scientific-educational. Create one photorealistic editorial photograph for a Korean elementary science workbook, landscape 3:2, no collage. A clean transparent beaker half filled with room-temperature clear water on a stable classroom table. A real stainless steel digital temperature sensor probe held upright by a laboratory clamp, sensing tip fully submerged near the center of the water and visibly separated from the bottom and every wall. Cable leads to a small real display turned away so NO numerals are legible. Show the entire safe apparatus including water surface, gap below the probe, retort stand and stable beaker base. Soft natural daylight, pale neutral classroom background, realistic glass refraction, matte surfaces, natural object proportions, crisp educational detail. No people, no hands, no heat source, no steam, no arrows, no labels, no letters or numbers anywhere, no illustration lines, no diagram, no decorative glow. Image is an illustrative setup, not a claim of actual temperature measurement.

Use-case: scientific-educational. One photorealistic educational laboratory photograph for an elementary science workbook, landscape 3:2. Safe heat-transfer observation apparatus on a stable tray: a small open thin-walled stainless steel cup, containing clear water, sits upright inside a larger transparent open beaker partly filled with clear water. Water in the outer beaker surrounds the outside of the metal cup; NO mixing or pouring between the two water samples. Inner cup rim is clearly well above the outside water level and stable. Two separate slim stainless temperature probes are securely clamped: one sensing tip inside the inner cup water, the other sensing tip in the outer beaker water outside the cup. Both sensing tips suspended in their respective water without touching walls or bases. Display backs face camera or displays outside frame, no legible values. Realistic water/glass/metal textures, bright neutral classroom, natural daylight, no people, no hands, no flame, no steam, no arrows, no labels, no text or numerals, no line diagram, no collage. Make the metal cup wall and separation of two water samples unambiguous.

Use-case: scientific-educational. One landscape 3:2 photorealistic elementary science workbook photograph. Teacher-prepared apparatus for comparing conduction under controlled conditions: three flat narrow rectangular strips of equal visible length and width hang vertically side by side from a sturdy horizontal wooden support over one wide clear vessel of water. One strip is matte copper, one is brushed aluminum, one is plain opaque plastic. Each strip lower end is immersed to the same small depth in the same water bath; most of each strip extends dry above the water. The support holds the upper ends safely and keeps strips separated. Each dry part has three identical small dark thermochromic indicator squares at matching heights; all indicators are initially the same dark color, no changed colors or conclusions. Entire apparatus clearly visible, stable base, real classroom tabletop, natural daylight, tactile material differences, real photography style. No heat source or flame, no hands, no people, no numeric scale, no numbers, no letters, no labels, no arrows, no extra diagram or collage, no glowing heat effects. This is explanatory apparatus photography, not measurement evidence.

Use-case: scientific-educational. One photorealistic classroom science apparatus photograph, landscape 3:2, no collage or illustration. A wide transparent borosilicate beaker with clear water on a stable small teacher-controlled electric warming plate. No visible controls, text or numerals. Inside the water, a small diffuse reddish food-color plume rises from near the bottom on one side and gently curls sideways near the surface; remaining water mostly clear. The dye is dissolved in the water, not smoke and not a solid tube, not sharp graphic arrows. No boiling bubbles, no steam, no flame, no glowing heat. Whole glass vessel and water surface and supporting base visible, pale neutral classroom background, realistic liquid refraction and reflections, natural daylight, crisp educational editorial photography. No hands or people, no labels, no numerals, no arrows. Explanatory illustration of a teacher demonstration, not a documented experiment or real temperature result. Do not depict any student manipulating hot apparatus.

Use-case: scientific-educational. Create a landscape 3:2 photorealistic editorial photo of a quiet bright elementary classroom interior. The educational subject is safe placement of heating/cooling equipment and air measurement positions: a modern white wall mounted split air conditioner high on the wall and a white enclosed stationary radiator/convector low on that wall; both clearly visible, placed with normal clearance, neither glowing, no open flame. Ordinary school desks neatly in foreground, natural window light, no people, no motion lines, no smoke, no visible colored air, no arrows, no diagram, no collage. No readable brand, text, temperature displays, labels or numerals. Tactile realistic architecture and photographic perspective. Picture shows equipment positions only, it must NOT pretend to visibly photograph invisible air circulation or actual heat measurements.

Use-case: scientific-educational. One landscape 3:2 photorealistic elementary science educational photograph of a safe sunlight absorption comparison setup. On a level pale classroom table by a window, two equal-size same-thickness matte rectangular paper sheets, one black and one white, lie flat side by side on identical thin plain cardboard supports. The SAME broad uninterrupted patch of sunlight illuminates BOTH entire sheets evenly; neither sheet is in shadow or overlapping the other. One small identical temperature sensor rests in the same relative center position on each sheet, secured identically with tiny clear tape; plain fine sensor cables lead outside the image, no displays. No magnifying glass, no focused beam, no lamp, no flame, no hands or people. Natural sunlight and realistic paper texture, photo style, no drawing, no arrows, no heat-glow, no numbers or text anywhere. Apparatus only, no actual temperature outcomes claimed.

Use-case: scientific-educational. One photorealistic landscape 3:2 elementary science workbook photo of everyday insulation objects on a bright pale wooden table: a plain unbranded soft insulated lunch/cooler bag with its zip lid open and realistic padded inner lining visible, one plain closed water bottle standing inside, an identical closed water bottle standing outside next to the bag, and a folded natural cotton towel beside them. The bottles are identical and have no labels or marks. Both caps are closed. No ice, no food, no thermometer readings, no claims of which bottle is warmer. Photograph should clearly show the bag lining and wrapping materials, natural real fabric weave and bottle reflections, editorial education style, clean neutral room, no collage or line art, no arrows, no numbers, no labels, no text, no people. This is a material/structure explanatory still life, not evidence of achieved insulation performance.

Use-case: scientific-educational. One landscape 3:2 photorealistic classroom science workbook photograph of a student-style insulation prototype and comparison setup, no people. On a large stable shallow tray stand two identical plain clear reusable cups with flat plain lids; one cup is bare, the other has its side wall and bottom wrapped neatly with a thick natural beige cloth sleeve. Lid of each cup has one small neat hole through which one identical slim stainless temperature probe passes vertically into the water, with sensing tips away from base and side walls. Each cup contains clear water to the same middle height, water in bare cup visible; wrapped cup contents mostly hidden. Probe cables lead to small displays facing away outside the main frame, absolutely no readable values. Teacher-prepared apparatus, no sharp tools, no heat source, no flame, no steam, no hands. Crisp real fabric texture, real glass/plastic reflections, natural daylight and pale school background, no drawn arrows, no colored heat, no text, no numbers, no collage. Image shows only apparatus and wrapping, no invented outcome or claimed actual experiment.
